name: amfora
desc: Fancy terminal browser for the Gemini protocol
why: A terminal browser for the Gemini protocol, a small alternative internet worth a look even if it is one of several.

brief.what_it_is: Amfora is a terminal browser for the Gemini protocol, a small internet protocol that is separate from the Web. You give it a gemini:// address and it fetches and renders the page inside your terminal, with styled headings, links, tabs, bookmarks, and history. It also handles Gemini input prompts, client certificates, and TOFU certificate checks. Its output is text drawn in the terminal, and it can download pages or hand non-text files to other applications.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the aim is to be "the best looking [Gemini](https://geminiquickst.art/) client with the most features... all in the terminal." It is scoped to Gemini only and does not support Gopher or other non-Web protocols; the README points to Bombadillo for those.
brief.how_it_works: Amfora is written in Go. It uses cview, a fork of tview, for the terminal interface, with tcell underneath for low-level terminal control. It uses the author's forked go-gemini library for the protocol, and Viper for configuration and TOFU certificate storage. Feed support covers RSS, Atom, and JSON Feed, and page subscriptions notify you when a page changes.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew needs only brew install amfora. Other routes: download a binary from the GitHub releases page and make it executable with chmod +x on Unix. On Windows, you may need to choose 'Advanced > Run anyway' after double-clicking. Amfora is also in many Linux distributions and on Scoop for Windows. MacPorts is available with sudo port install amfora. On Termux (Android), install Amfora, run pkg install proot, and launch the binary through termux-chroot. To build from source, you need Go 1.15 or later and GNU Make; the Makefile does not target Windows. Run make, then sudo make install for a system-wide install. Arch users can install amfora-git from the AUR, and macOS users can run brew install --HEAD amfora for the latest commit. The README recommends Windows Terminal with UTF-8 on Windows. No account or API key is mentioned. Usage and configuration are documented in the project wiki.
brief.standout: It targets a niche protocol and aims to be the most polished Gemini client in a terminal, with tabs, theming, feed subscriptions, and a claimed pass of two client torture tests. It is also honest about its own status: the author has put it into maintenance mode.
brief.status: Maintenance mode, according to the README. The author says bug fixes will be made or merged when possible and that feature PRs from others may be merged slowly, with a link to a 2023/08 blog post explaining the decision. The README gives no release date or last-commit date, so I cannot say how recently it was released.
brief.caveats: The project is in maintenance mode, so new features are unlikely. On Windows, some application colors may not display correctly, though the README says all functionality still works; it recommends Windows Terminal with UTF-8. The README does not support Gopher or other non-Web protocols. On Termux, it does not run without proot and termux-chroot. The Makefile does not target Windows. The README says the MacPorts port is community-maintained. The license is GPL v3.0. The brew caveats field was empty.
